cards.back: The **weighted mean mass** of an atom of an element compared with $\frac{1}{12}$ of the mass of an atom of **carbon-12**.

cards.front: How many particles are in one mole? What is this number called?
Define first ionisation energy. Write the equation for sodium.
cards.back:
The energy needed to remove **one electron** from **each atom** in **one mole of gaseous atoms** to form one mole of **gaseous 1+ ions**.
$$\ce{Na(g) -> Na+(g) + e-}$$
Exam tip: always include the **(g)** state symbols.
The **power of an atom to attract the bonding pair of electrons** in a **covalent bond** towards itself.

cards.front: Write the ideal gas equation with the units each quantity must be in.
cards.back:
$$pV = nRT$$
$p$ in **Pa**, $V$ in **m$^3$**, $T$ in **K**, and $R = 8.31\ \text{J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$.
Exam trap: cm$^3$ to m$^3$ is **$\times 10^{-6}$**, and °C to K is **+ 273**.

cards.front: Define standard enthalpy change of formation, $\Delta H_\text{f}^{\ominus}$.
cards.back: The enthalpy change when **one mole of a compound** is formed from its **elements in their standard states** under **standard conditions** (298 K, 101 kPa).

cards.front: Define standard enthalpy change of combustion, $\Delta H_\text{c}^{\ominus}$.
cards.back: The enthalpy change when **one mole of a substance** is **burned completely in excess oxygen** under **standard conditions** (298 K, 101 kPa).

cards.front: Define oxidation in terms of electrons and oxidation number.
cards.back: Oxidation is **loss of electrons**, or an **increase in oxidation number**.
If a **change** is made to a system in **dynamic equilibrium**, the **position of equilibrium shifts** to **minimise the change**.

cards.front: Define a Brønsted–Lowry acid and a Brønsted–Lowry base.
cards.back:
An **acid** is a **proton ($\ce{H+}$) donor**.
A **base** is a **proton ($\ce{H+}$) acceptor**.
The **minimum energy** that colliding particles must have for a **successful collision** (for the reaction to occur).

cards.front: How does a catalyst increase the rate of a reaction?
cards.back:
It provides an **alternative reaction pathway** with a **lower activation energy**.
So **more particles have energy $\geq E_\text{a}$**, and the **frequency of successful collisions** increases.
The catalyst is **chemically unchanged** at the end.
